questions.question: During which movement did Chauri-Chaura incident happen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-cooperation movement.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Non-cooperation movement:**

 
 
• It was a civil disobedience movement launched in British India in 1920 by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• **The movement was based on the principle of non-violent resistance and was aimed at pressurizing the British government to grant India independence.**
 
• The movement involved a boycott of British goods, institutions, and services, as well as the resignation of Indians from government jobs and titles.
 
• **The Chauri Chaura incident happened during the Non-cooperation movement.**
 
 
 
• **Chauri Chaura incident:-**
 
 
• The Chauri Chaura incident occurred on February 4, 1922, in the town of Chauri Chaura in the Gorakhpur district of the United Provinces (present-day Uttar Pradesh) in British India.
 
• **It was a violent incident between Indian protesters and British police that took place during the Non-cooperation movement.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quit India Movement: **

 
 
• **It was a civil disobedience movement launched in 1942 by the Indian National Congress. **
 
• The movement demanded the immediate withdrawal of the British from India.
 
• The British government responded by cracking down on the movement and arresting thousands of leaders and activists.
 
 
 
• **Champaran Movement: **
 
 
• **It was a civil disobedience movement launched in 1917 by Mahatma Gandhi to support the indigo farmers of Champaran district in Bihar. **
 
• The farmers were being forced to grow indigo at low prices and were subjected to various abuses by the indigo planters.
 
• Gandhi's intervention led to the establishment of a commission of inquiry, which recommended several reforms for the benefit of the farmers.
 
 
 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement: **
 
 
• **It was a civil disobedience movement launched in 1930 by Mahatma Gandhi. **
 
• The movement was aimed at challenging the British Salt Act, which imposed a tax on salt. Gandhi led a march to the sea, where he made salt illegally, in defiance of the law.
 
• The movement spread across India and involved millions of people.

questions.question: As per Consumer Protection Rules, 2021, National Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds _________.

• **The Consumer Protection Rules, 2021 were notified by the Central Government on July 22, 2021. **

• **As per Consumer Protection Rules, 2021, National Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds two crore rupees.**
 
• The **previous pecuniary jurisdiction of the National Commission was one crore rupees, but it was increased to two crore rupees by the Consumer Protection Rules, 2021**.
 
• This means that consumers can now file complaints with the National Commission for grievances involving goods or services worth more than two crore rupees.

• It can also issue directions to businesses to stop unfair practices.

questions.question: _________ is associated with spoilage, development of off-flavors, deterioration of textures, discoloration and loss of nutritional value.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**food deterioration**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Food deterioration:-**

__
 
• **It is a natural process that occurs over time in all foods. **
 
• **It is caused by a variety of factors, including:**
 
 
• **Microorganisms**: Bacteria, yeasts, and molds can grow on food and cause it to spoil.
 
• **Enzymes**: Enzymes are naturally occurring proteins that speed up chemical reactions. In food, enzymes can cause food to break down and spoil.
 
• **Oxygen**: Oxygen can cause food to oxidize and become rancid.
 
• **Light**: Light can cause food to discolor and lose nutrients.
 
• **Temperature**: Temperature can affect the rate of food deterioration. Food spoils more quickly at warm temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Food deterioration can cause a variety of problems, including:**
 
 
• **Spoilage**: Spoiled food is unsafe to eat and can cause food poisoning.
 
• **Off-flavors**: Food that is starting to deteriorate may develop off-flavors, such as sourness, bitterness, or staleness.
 
• **Deterioration of textures**: Food that is deteriorating may become slimy, mushy, or tough.
 
• **Discoloration**: Food that is deteriorating may change color, such as browning or fading.
 
• **Loss of nutritional value: **Food that is deteriorating may lose some of its nutrients.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Food processing:-**

 
 
• It can be any method used to turn raw food into food products.
 
• It can involve one or a combination of the following: washing, chopping, pasteurizing, freezing, fermenting, packaging, and more.
 
 
 
• **Food preservation:-**
 
 
• It is the process of treating and handling food to prevent or slow down its spoilage.

questions.question: If a number 'a' is divisible by 18 and another number 'b' is divisible by 12, then (a² - b²) is divisible by :
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the numbers be their smallest positive multiples: a = 18 and b = 12.

(a² − b²) = 18² − 12² = 324 − 144 = 180.

Checking the given options, 180 is divisible by both 30 and 36.

Now, test for another multiple: let a = 18 and b = 24.

(a² − b²) = 18² − 24² = 324 − 576 = −252, which is divisible by 36 but not 30.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number a is divisible by 18, and number b is divisible by 12.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let a = 18x (where x is an integer)

⇒ Let b = 12y (where y is an integer)

⇒ a² = (18x)²

⇒ a² = 324x²

⇒ b² = (12y)²

⇒ b² = 144y²

⇒ a² − b² = 324x² − 144y²

⇒ Taking the highest common factor from both numerical coefficients:

⇒ 324 = 36 × 9

⇒ 144 = 36 × 4

⇒ a² − b² = 36(9x² − 4y²)

⇒ Since x and y are integers, the term (9x² − 4y²) will also evaluate to an integer.

⇒ Hence, the entire expression is a direct multiple of 36 and will always be divisible by 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility of an Expression

If an algebraic expression can be rewritten as a multiple of an integer k, i.e., N = k × m (where m is an integer), then N is always completely divisible by k and all the factors of k.

Difference of Squares

The identity a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) is highly useful for finding common factors of quadratic differences without manually calculating the large squares directly.

Properties of Common Divisors

The highest constant value that divides an algebraic expression axⁿ − byⁿ for all integer values of variables x and y is simply the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of the coefficients a and b.
